clue.text: Public address in this state shortly — where's 10?

definitions.text: Public address in this state shortly — where's 10?

parts.words: Public address in this state shortly — where's 10?
parts.note: the usual short form of this US state is the same pair of letters as the abbreviation for a public address system, and the state is where the town at 10 stands

explanation.surface: Someone asks over the loudspeaker where a particular small town might be found.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no buildable wordplay: the clue rests on PA being both 'public address' and the postal abbreviation of the state, while 'where's 10?' points to the state containing Punxsutawney.
explanation.definitionFit: Punxsutawney, the town at 10, lies in this northeastern US state, and PA is its standard postal abbreviation.

clue.text: Female 10's 26 part 1's half daft about

indicators.note: half of the four-letter name means its first two letters only

parts.note: the Groundhog of Punxsutawney (10) on Groundhog Day (26) is known as Phil

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for daft is read backwards

parts.note: daft means silly

explanation.surface: A muddled reference to a woman being half crazy about something.
explanation.walkthrough: '10's 26 part 1' means the first word of the famous groundhog's name, Punxsutawney Phil; its first half gives PH. 'about' turns SILLY into YLLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllis is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a female.

clue.text: Small children taking exercise during spring outing — no force required

indicators.note: during means the exercise letters sit within the other letters
an outing takes the letters out of their order, so the remains of spring are rearranged
no means the letter for force is missing from the word spring

parts.note: g is the symbol for force due to gravity, as in g-force
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Youngsters are taken on a springtime trip, with physical effort apparently unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no force' drops G, the g-force symbol, giving SPRIN, which 'outing' rearranges to NIPRS; 'during' puts the exercise inside. 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippers is informal British slang for small children or kids.

clue.text: Deferred start to spring? Part of America awaited judgment

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of spring is used

parts.note: the US, the United States, is a part of the Americas
to pend is to remain undecided, awaiting judgment

explanation.surface: A question about whether spring has been postponed, then a picture of an American region waiting for a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspended has been put off or postponed, the same as deferred.

clue.text: Runs cut off by opponents during play

parts.note: to lop is to cut off a branch
in bridge play East and South sit on opposing sides, so E and S are opponents

explanation.surface: A game story where players are blocked by the other side mid-match.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the partnerships are North-South and East-West, so E and S are a pair of opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy strides, so lopes means runs.

clue.text: "The greatest" newspaper lifted hearts in an Indian city

parts.note: boxer Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a rag is a low-quality newspaper
H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A tabloid praising a champion boxer is said to have cheered people in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns RAG upwards, giving GAR in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Aligarh is a city in Uttar Pradesh, northern India, famous for its Muslim university.

clue.text: Bard repeatedly denied bearing malice

indicators.note: denied means the bearing letter is taken away from what precedes it
repeatedly means the name for the Bard is written twice

parts.note: the Bard is Shakespeare, whose first name was Will
W, west, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Shakespeare, refused again and again, is said to hold a grudge.
explanation.walkthrough: WILL written twice gives WILLWILL; 'denied' removes one W, the bearing West, from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is a phrase for hostility or spite, a direct equivalent of malice.

clue.text: Attempt to get on Big Brother list initially, before turning bonkers in the home of 10's 26 part 1

parts.note: a go is an attempt
BB is a common abbreviation for Big Brother

indicators.note: initially means just the opening letter of list
turning means the letters of bonkers are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get onto a reality TV show's list before going mad in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges BONKERS to ERSKNOB. Gobbler's Knob is the hill at Punxsutawney where Phil the groundhog makes his forecast each year.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbler's Knob is the small hill outside Punxsutawney where the forecasting groundhog Phil lives and appears on 2 February.

clue.text: A big rise in the camera business?

definitions.meaning: a big rise is a lofty mountain, the home of the Greek gods
a Japanese manufacturer of cameras and optics shares the mountain's name

explanation.surface: A question about a sharp increase in camera sales.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Olympus is Greece's highest peak and also the name of a well-known Japanese camera company.

clue.text: Boy giving 10's 26 part 1 backchat

parts.note: the Punxsutawney groundhog of Groundhog Day is called Phil
lip is cheeky talk or backchat

explanation.surface: A lad cheeks the famous groundhog.
explanation.definitionFit: Phillip is a male given name, so it serves for a boy.

clue.text: At sun-up we cross New York, off to 26's location

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and must be rearranged

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: At dawn a group traverses New York state on their way to a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ATSUNUPWE with X and NY. Groundhog Day is famously celebrated in this Pennsylvania town.
explanation.definitionFit: Punxsutawney in Pennsylvania is where the best-known Groundhog Day ceremony takes place every 2 February.

clue.text: Think to contradict verdict initially given on the second of February

parts.note: to belie is to contradict or give the lie to

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of verdict
the second of picks the letter in second position of February

explanation.surface: A ruling made on Groundhog Day, 2 February, is thought worth disputing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the second of February' looks like the date of Groundhog Day, the theme, but it simply picks the second letter, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To believe is to think or hold an opinion, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: "Silence of the Birds", by GB playwright?

parts.note: sh is a call for silence
avian means of or relating to birds

explanation.surface: A title like a film, "Silence of the Birds", supposedly written by a British dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: GB is George Bernard Shaw, the Irish-born playwright; the clue also hints at the film title The Silence of the Lambs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shavian is the adjective for George Bernard Shaw, so a work by that playwright is Shavian.

clue.text: First signs of early spring … snowdrop's opening … first signs of early spring … snowdrop's opening repeatedly …

definitions.text: First signs of early spring … snowdrop's opening … first signs of early spring … snowdrop's opening repeatedly …

parts.words: First signs of early spring … snowdrop's opening … first signs of early spring … snowdrop's opening repeatedly …
parts.note: the first letters of spring and snowdrop's are both the letter S, and the clue repeats itself like the day that keeps recurring in the film

explanation.surface: A nature diary stuck in a loop, recording the first snowdrops of spring over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is a cryptic definition: the opening letters of 'spring' and 'snowdrop's' are each S, and the repetition mimics the time loop of Groundhog Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Esses is the plural spelling of the letter S, the letter that begins spring and snowdrop.

clue.text: Wife has her lumps regularly checked out for diseased growths

parts.note: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' means my wife

indicators.note: regularly checked out means every other letter of her lumps is taken

explanation.surface: A woman with lumps has them examined at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'her lumps' gives ELMS. 'Dutch' for wife is old London (Cockney) slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Dutch elms are the trees ravaged by Dutch elm disease, so they are diseased growths.

clue.text: Top English hotel re-ordered an 8 accessory?

indicators.note: re-ordered means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A top English hotel is booked again.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto lens is an add-on for a camera such as one made by Olympus (8).

clue.text: Piano played badly? That's not unknown with this piano piece

parts.note: in music piano means soft

indicators.note: badly means the remaining letters are jumbled
not means the unknown letter is left out of played

parts.note: y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A remark that a piano performance was poor, though not entirely unfamiliar.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAYED without Y leaves PLAED, which 'badly' rearranges to PEDAL. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft pedal is a pedal on a piano that quietens the tone, so a part of the instrument.

clue.text: Bum ref upset outside left — he dropped the ball

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the other letter
upset means the letters of bum ref are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A useless referee is annoyed by the left winger who lost possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges BUMREF to FUMBER, and 'outside' places it round L.
explanation.definitionFit: A fumbler is someone who handles clumsily and lets the ball slip, as in American football.

clue.text: Upstart assistant to king and goddess, briefly

parts.note: a PA is a personal assistant
R is short for rex, king

indicators.note: briefly means the goddess's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Venus is the Roman goddess of love

explanation.surface: A social climber serves a monarch and a goddess for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is a newly rich social climber, an upstart.

clue.text: Bit of a problem, meteorologically, for a small creature

indicators.note: bit of says only a portion of the words that follow is used

explanation.surface: A weather problem affects a little animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'problEM METeorologically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmet is an old or dialect word for an ant, a small creature.

clue.text: Up before court? Balls!

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Ed Balls is a British former Labour politician

explanation.surface: Someone is summoned to court and swears in exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls!' reads as an expletive, but it is the surname of Ed Balls, a Labour cabinet minister and later TV personality, giving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To up something can mean to raise it, and erected means raised or put up.

clue.text: My lot is suffering with damp

indicators.note: suffering suggests the words are in distress and so broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that one's lot is to suffer in wet conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Moistly is an adverb meaning in a damp manner, as 'with damp' describes.

clue.text: One ruling that results from endless repeats of 26?

definitions.meaning: a governor of a nome, a province of ancient or modern Egypt or Greece
if 2 February repeated forever, as in the film, the third month would never arrive

explanation.surface: A ruler emerges from a film played on an infinite loop.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as NO MARCH: endlessly repeated Groundhog Days mean March never comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomarch rules a nome, an administrative district in Egypt or Greece, so one ruling.

clue.text: Wearing stockings, say, in those days

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Back then people wore stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'tHOSE Days'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose are stockings or tights, so hosed means wearing such legwear.

clue.text: Early showing of 10's leader before official inspection

indicators.note: before means the first piece is placed ahead of the second

parts.note: the leading letter of the town at 10 is P
a review is a formal inspection

explanation.surface: An early screening of a town's mayor ahead of an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: '10's leader' is the first letter of PUNXSUTAWNEY, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is a showing of a film or play before its general release.

clue.text: French letters found in sleeping quarters

definitions.meaning: the French word for notes or letters, as in ...-doux, love letters

explanation.surface: Condoms, slang French letters, discovered in a dormitory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French letters' is British slang for condoms, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Billets are soldiers' lodgings, and billet is also French for a note or letter.

clue.text: Month intrinsically better for a female boat crew?

parts.note: Oct is short for October

indicators.note: intrinsically means only the inside letters of better are used

explanation.surface: A month that is fundamentally better for women's rowing.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew; an octet with the feminine '-ette' ending makes a jokey female crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Octette is a variant of octet, a group of eight, and the -ette ending suggests a female crew of eight rowers.

clue.text: Film homosexual eating sandwich — one with ham in it, and a little duck

indicators.note: eating means the gay letters enclose the rest

parts.note: gay means homosexual
a round is a sandwich made from two slices of bread
a hog is a pig, which carries ham on its body
D is short for duck, a zero score in cricket

explanation.surface: A gay man eats a ham sandwich and a bit of duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one with ham in it' sounds like a filled sandwich but is the pig itself. 'a' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundhog Day is the 1993 comedy in which Bill Murray relives the same day repeatedly.
